what: The verdicts the fourth project (kvparse, plan node K1) is expected to get on its ten Rule lines, which are the rule pack validated-input@1 instantiated with the words of clausebook/local/kvparse.yaml. Written and committed BEFORE the pipeline was run on them. Compared with out/graph.json by `python3 kvparse/check_expected.py` (run from clausal/, after ./run.sh).

Rule.kvparse_rules.vi_1.why: believed true (every index is in range, no subtraction below zero); no proof is supplied: it needs a loop invariant

Rule.kvparse_rules.vi_2.why: believed true; no proof is supplied: it is the agreement of the loop with the specification's tokeniser

Rule.kvparse_rules.vi_3.why: believed true; no proof is supplied (as VI-2)

Rule.kvparse_rules.vi_4.why: true, and the length check is before the loop: a hand-written proof of the generated obligation is to be supplied

Rule.kvparse_rules.vi_5.why: true of EVERY operation with this answer type: a record has two keys, so the count is at most 2 whatever the code does. The proof does not look at the code. Reported as a rule that says nothing about this parser

Rule.kvparse_rules.vi_6.why: believed true; no proof is supplied (as VI-2). The half 'changes nothing' holds by construction: the parser is read, never written

Rule.kvparse_rules.vi_7b.why: believed true (the format is canonical: one input per record); no proof is supplied

Rule.kvparse_rules.vi_8.why: believed true; no proof is supplied

Rule.kvparse_rules.vi_9.why: believed true; no proof is supplied

Rule.kvparse_rules.vi_10.why: believed true; no proof is supplied: it is the whole correctness of the parser

functions.why: input coverage is computed from proved universal SCENARIOS of the old glossary; kvparse has Rule lines only and no trivial-model entry, so no suite adequacy verdict either (as for the counter)

no_other_verdict: no other rule or scenario verdict of out/graph.json may name kvparse
